chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sadir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: On the Day of Resurrection, the creatures will be called by their mothers' names, except us and our Shia, for there is no adultery among us.
ai.seo_question: Why are the Shia and Ahl al-Bayt exempt from being called by their mothers' names on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Sifat al-Shia tradition, this hadith highlights the unique ontological status of the Ahl al-Bayt and their faithful followers, distinguishing them from the general populace who are identified by their mothers' names due to the prevalence of uncertain paternity (sifah). The exemption signifies a divine guarantee of pure, unbroken lineage for the Imams and a spiritual purity for the Shia, reflecting their distinct identity in the eschatological gathering. This concept underscores the theological emphasis on lineage and purity as markers of divine favor and closeness to God.

en.badr-shahin: Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Mohammed bin Yahya bin Sadir

that Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, all the creatures will be called with the names of their mothers. We, as well as our Shia, are not bound by this act, because we are saved from adultery."
